question.explanation: 밑줄 (A)의 골격은 'an attachment(선행사, 단수) + that(주격 관계대명사) + is shown(관계절 동사)'이다. 관계절의 동사는 선행사 an attachment의 수에 일치해야 하므로 단수 be동사 is가 와야 하는데, 제시된 'are shown'은 복수 동사로 수일치가 깨져 비문이다. 따라서 'that are shown'은 'that is shown'으로 고쳐야 한다. attachment 앞의 여러 명사(background 등)에 이끌려 복수로 오인하기 쉬우므로 진짜 선행사가 무엇인지 파악하는 것이 핵심이다.
keyPoints: (A) 관계대명사절 수일치 — 선행사 an attachment(단수)에 맞춰 관계절 동사도 단수 is가 되어야 한다
(B) 관계부사 where — 장소 선행사 뒤 완전한 절을 이끄는 구조로 적절하다
(E) 주어-동사 수일치 — 단수 주어 his sculpture에 맞춰 transcends로 수일치되어 있다
question.passageWithMarkers: Allan Houser created contemporary Apache sculpture. As a child, he listened to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo. This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment __(A) that are shown__ in his artwork. Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, __(B) where he worked__ as a freelance artist. During World War II, he traveled to California, __(C) where he became__ interested in the media of sculpture. He created works in a variety of styles and __(D) mastered__ bronze, metal, and stone sculpture. Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly rooted in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers. He drew inspiration from both past and present, but like all successful artists, his sculpture __(E) transcends__ race and language. The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be appreciated by anyone, regardless of his or her background.

passageText: Allan Houser created contemporary Apache sculpture. As a child, he listened to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo. This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is shown in his artwork. Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, where he worked as a freelance artist. During World War II, he traveled to California, where he became interested in the media of sculpture. He created works in a variety of styles and mastered bronze, metal, and stone sculpture. Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly rooted in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers. He drew inspiration from both past and present, but like all successful artists, his sculpture transcends race and language. The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be appreciated by anyone, regardless of his or her background.

passageText: We all enjoy the pleasure of being left alone with a good book. But sometimes after several hours of immersion we lift our heads and look around, suddenly struck by the quiet, the absence of others. In this situation, we are suffering from reading-induced loneliness. The solution is to read in the company of other people who are reading - whether in a public space such as a café or a library, or in your own home, with your reading friend or partner at the other end of the sofa. Next time you look up, you'll see someone else similarly immersed, and you won't feel alone at all. Reading can be sociable. Consider joining a reading group in which everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel. Reading a book collaboratively is a wonderful way to share an otherwise internal and solitary experience.

passageText: We tend to think of technology as shiny tools and gadgets. Even if we acknowledge that technology can exist in disembodied form, such as software, we tend not to include in this category paintings, literature, music, dance, poetry, and the arts in general. But we should. If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX qualifies as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must qualify as well. They both can change our behavior, alter the course of events, or enable future inventions. A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony, then, are in the same category as Google's search engine and the smartphone: They are something useful produced by a mind. We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies responsible for a Lord of the Rings movie. The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures. Both are useful works of the human imagination. Both influence audiences powerfully. Both are technological.

passageText: The human brain is wired to look for threats - a trait that kept us alive when we were living on the savannas but that can prevent happiness in our modern lives. This so-called "negativity bias" can keep you focused on what's going wrong (which explains why complaining is such a popular pastime). To break out of this neural rut, train yourself to acknowledge when things go right. If you keep a calendar or a journal, make a point to write down what went well. If you're more of a verbal processor, start your conversations with friends by sharing a recent win (anything that gives you that yesssss feeling). Where the mind goes, reality follows. The more you appreciate life, the more reasons you have to celebrate it.

wrongOptionExplanations.(B): rather than은 앞의 We reconstruct라는 동사와 대비되는 대상을 이끄는데, than 뒤에 동명사 retrieving을 써서 reconstruct(동사원형에 상응)와 병렬적으로 대비시키는 관용 표현이므로 적절하다.

keyPoints: (C) 병렬구조 — 관계대명사 who의 선행사 People에 대해 and로 연결된 두 정동사 lack과 remember는 형태가 일치해야 한다

question.passageWithMarkers: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. __(A) We recode__ what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories __(B) rather than retrieving__ the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and __(C) remembering__ everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. passageText: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 문장의 주어 자리에 오는 동명사로서 'making time for exercise'가 하나의 명사구를 이루어 단수 주어 역할을 하므로 어법상 옳다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 주어 핵이 'the beauty'로 단수이므로 단수동사 'comes'가 수일치하여 옳다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 주어 'it'(비인칭 주어로 washing dishes를 가리킴)에 대한 be동사의 단수형으로 축약형 'it's'는 어법상 옳다.

question.explanation: (D) "to take out"는 어법상 틀린 표현이며 "taking out"로 고쳐야 한다. 정답 문장은 'Whether it's washing dishes or taking out the trash, these tasks are an essential part of daily life'로, whether A or B 구조에서 A자리 'washing'(동명사)과 B자리가 등위접속사 or로 병렬 연결된다. 지문에 제시된 'to take out'은 부정사 형태로 A자리의 동명사와 형태가 불일치하여 병렬 구조가 깨지므로 비문이다. 따라서 동명사 형태인 'taking out'으로 고쳐야 병렬 구조가 완성된다. 학생들은 whether절 내부라 부정사도 가능하다고 오판할 수 있으나, 이미 A자리가 동명사로 고정되어 있으므로 B자리도 동일 형태를 따라야 한다.
keyPoints: (D) 병렬구조 — whether A or B 구조에서 A(washing)와 B(taking out)는 동일한 동명사 형태로 병렬되어야 한다
(A) 동명사 주어 — making이 명사구를 이루어 단수 주어로 기능하는지 확인해야 한다
(E) 동명사 주어 — Incorporating이 문장 전체의 주어 역할을 하며 단수동사와 연결되는지 확인해야 한다
question.passageWithMarkers: For many of us, __(A) making__ time for exercise __(B) is__ a continuing challenge. Between work commitments and family obligations, it often feels like there's no room in our packed schedules for a dedicated workout. But what if the workout came to you, right in the midst of your daily routine? That's where the beauty of integrating mini-exercises into household chores __(C) comes__ into play. Let's be realistic; chores are inevitable. Whether it's washing dishes or __(D) to take out__ the trash, these tasks are an essential part of daily life. But rather than viewing chores as purely obligatory activities, why not seize these moments as opportunities for physical activity? For instance, practice squats or engage in some wall push-ups as you wait for your morning kettle to boil. __(E) Incorporating__ quick exercises into your daily chores can improve your health.

passageText: For many of us, making time for exercise is a continuing challenge. Between work commitments and family obligations, it often feels like there's no room in our packed schedules for a dedicated workout. But what if the workout came to you, right in the midst of your daily routine? That's where the beauty of integrating mini-exercises into household chores comes into play. Let's be realistic; chores are inevitable. Whether it's washing dishes or taking out the trash, these tasks are an essential part of daily life. But rather than viewing chores as purely obligatory activities, why not seize these moments as opportunities for physical activity? For instance, practice squats or engage in some wall push-ups as you wait for your morning kettle to boil. Incorporating quick exercises into your daily chores can improve your health.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E) 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We have all had the experience of suddenly noticing that a source of constant background noise

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Your auditory areas were predicting its continuation, moment after moment, and as long as the noise didn't change

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: By ceasing, it violated your prediction and attracted your attention.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Right after New York City stopped running elevated trains, people called the police in the middle of the night

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: They tended to call around the time the trains used to run past their apartments.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 주어 We에 맞춰 현재완료 have가 쓰였고 all은 부사로 주어와 동사 사이에 삽입된 형태이므로 수일치와 시제 모두 올바르다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): Your auditory areas가 스스로 예측하는 행위의 주체이므로 능동의 과거진행 were predicting이 적절하며 뒤에 목적어 its continuation이 있어 수동태로 바꿀 이유가 없다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): stop은 동명사를 목적어로 취해 '~하는 것을 멈추다'라는 뜻을 나타내므로 stopped running은 올바른 형태이다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): '예전에 ~했다'는 과거의 습관·상태를 나타내는 used to 뒤에는 동사원형이 와야 하므로 used to run은 올바르다.

question.explanation: (C) "By to cease"는 어법상 틀린 표현이며 "By ceasing"로 고쳐야 한다. 밑줄 (C)의 골격은 'By ceasing, it violated your prediction'으로, 전치사 By의 목적어 자리에 동명사 ceasing이 와야 한다. 따라서 By 뒤에는 동명사 ceasing을 그대로 써야 한다. 학생들은 to cease와 ceasing이 의미상 비슷해 보여 혼동할 수 있으나, 전치사 뒤 자리라는 통사적 조건이 결정적 판단 기준이다.
keyPoints: (C) to-v/v-ing — 전치사 By 뒤에는 동명사만 목적어로 올 수 있음
(D) 정·준동사 — stop 뒤에 동명사가 오면 '~하기를 멈추다'라는 뜻이 되어 문맥상 적절함
(E) 정·준동사 — used to 뒤에는 동사원형이 와야 과거의 습관을 나타냄
question.passageWithMarkers: We __(A) have all had__ the experience of suddenly noticing that a source of constant background noise, such as a distant jackhammer or music from a store, has just ceased - yet we hadn't noticed the sound while it was ongoing. Your auditory areas __(B) were predicting__ its continuation, moment after moment, and as long as the noise didn't change you paid it no attention. __(C) By to cease__, it violated your prediction and attracted your attention. Here's a historical example. Right after New York City __(D) stopped running__ elevated trains, people called the police in the middle of the night claiming that something woke them up. They tended to call around the time the trains __(E) used to run__ past their apartments.

passageText: We have all had the experience of suddenly noticing that a source of constant background noise, such as a distant jackhammer or music from a store, has just ceased - yet we hadn't noticed the sound while it was ongoing. Your auditory areas were predicting its continuation, moment after moment, and as long as the noise didn't change you paid it no attention. By ceasing, it violated your prediction and attracted your attention. Here's a historical example. Right after New York City stopped running elevated trains, people called the police in the middle of the night claiming that something woke them up. They tended to call around the time the trains used to run past their apartments.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E) 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The fast pace of today's lifestyle has us piling one thing on top of another.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: you should know that multitasking doesn't save any time

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: It doesn't take up any more time than it would when done with your phone pressed to your ear.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Focus on one task at a time, and you'll accomplish each task better, and probably faster.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Focus on one task at a time, and you'll accomplish each task better, and probably faster.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 사역동사 have는 'have+목적어+동사원형/v-ing' 구조를 취하는데, 목적어 us와 pile의 관계가 능동(우리가 쌓는 것)이므로 v-ing 형태인 piling이 올바르게 쓰였다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 주어 multitasking은 단수 취급되는 동명사 주어이므로 조동사 does의 부정형 doesn't와 동사원형 save가 결합한 doesn't save는 수일치상 올바르다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): Focus on one task at a time은 명령문으로 동사원형 Focus로 시작하며, and로 이어진 you'll accomplish 절과 등위 연결되어 구조상 문제가 없다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 조동사 will 뒤에는 동사원형이 와야 하므로 you'll accomplish는 will+accomplish의 형태로 어법상 올바르다.

question.explanation: 밑줄 친 (C) pressing은 'with+명사+분사' 구문에서 명사 your phone과 분사의 의미관계를 나타낸다. your phone은 누르는 행위를 하는 주체가 아니라 귀에 눌려지는 대상이므로 수동관계이며, 능동형 v-ing인 pressing은 이 자리에서 비문이다. 따라서 과거분사 pressed로 고쳐 with your phone pressed to your ear(전화기가 귀에 눌린 채로)가 되어야 한다. 학생들은 with+명사+v-ing를 무조건 분사구문 공식으로 외워 능동형을 습관적으로 쓰기 쉬우므로 명사와 분사의 의미상 관계를 반드시 따져야 한다.
keyPoints: (C) 분사의 능동·수동 판별 — with+명사+분사 구문에서 명사가 동작의 대상이면 과거분사를 써야 한다
(A) 사역동사 목적격보어 — have+목적어+v-ing는 목적어와 동작이 능동관계일 때 사용한다
(E) 조동사 뒤 동사원형 — will 뒤에는 반드시 동사원형이 와야 한다
question.passageWithMarkers: The fast pace of today's lifestyle __(A) has us piling__ one thing on top of another. But you should know that multitasking __(B) doesn't save__ any time. Very often, multitasking only slows you down, contrary to popular belief. Give your whole focus to what you're doing at the moment no matter what it is. While doing the laundry, just do the laundry: Listen to the sound of the water as it fills the washing machine and feel the clothes in your hand. It doesn't take up any more time than it would when done with your phone __(C) pressing__ to your ear. The same applies to your work. __(D) Focus__ on one task at a time, and __(E) you'll accomplish__ each task better, and probably faster.

passageText: The fast pace of today's lifestyle has us piling one thing on top of another. But you should know that multitasking doesn't save any time. Very often, multitasking only slows you down, contrary to popular belief. Give your whole focus to what you're doing at the moment no matter what it is. While doing the laundry, just do the laundry: Listen to the sound of the water as it fills the washing machine and feel the clothes in your hand. It doesn't take up any more time than it would when done with your phone pressed to your ear. The same applies to your work. Focus on one task at a time, and you'll accomplish each task better, and probably faster.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E) 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: There is a critical factor that determines whether your choice will influence that of others

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: There is the leopard seal, for one, which likes to have penguins for a meal.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: If the pioneer survives, everyone else will follow suit.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: If it perishes, they'll turn away.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: One penguin's destiny alters the fate of all the others.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 관계대명사 that의 선행사는 단수명사 a critical factor이므로 단수동사 determines가 오는 것이 맞다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): if가 이끄는 단순 조건 부사절에서는 현재시제로 미래의 의미를 나타내므로 survives는 어법상 적절하다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): perish는 자동사로 수동태가 불가능하며 주어 it(the pioneer)이 3단수이므로 perishes로 쓰는 것이 옳다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 주어는 단수명사 One penguin's destiny이므로 3단수 동사 alters가 수일치상 올바르다.

question.explanation: (B) "to like"는 어법상 틀린 표현이며 "likes"로 고쳐야 한다. 밑줄 (B)가 포함된 문장은 'the leopard seal, for one, which likes to have penguins for a meal'로, 선행사 the leopard seal(단수)을 받는 주격 관계대명사 which 뒤에는 절의 정동사가 필요하다. 그런데 to like는 준동사(to부정사)이므로 관계사절에 술어가 존재하지 않아 문장이 성립하지 않는다. 따라서 to like를 정동사 likes로 고쳐야 한다. 학생들은 대신 (A)의 단수 주어 a critical factor와 determines의 일치, (E)의 One penguin's destiny와 alters의 일치를 헷갈려 정답으로 착각하기 쉽다.
keyPoints: (B) 관계사절 — 주격 관계대명사 which 뒤에는 정동사가 필요하며 준동사(to like)로 대체할 수 없다
(A) 수일치 — 단수 선행사 a critical factor에 단수동사 determines가 맞다
(E) 수일치 — 단수 주어 One penguin's destiny에 단수동사 alters가 맞다
question.passageWithMarkers: There is a critical factor that __(A) determines__ whether your choice will influence that of others: the visible consequences of the choice. Take the case of the Adélie penguins. They are often found strolling in large groups toward the edge of the water in search of food. Yet danger awaits in the icy-cold water. There is the leopard seal, for one, which __(B) to like__ to have penguins for a meal. What is an Adélie to do? The penguins' solution is to play the waiting game. They wait and wait and wait by the edge of the water until one of them gives up and jumps in. The moment that occurs, the rest of the penguins watch with anticipation to see what happens next. If the pioneer __(C) survives__, everyone else will follow suit. If it __(D) perishes__, they'll turn away. One penguin's destiny __(E) alters__ the fate of all the others. Their strategy, you could say, is "learn and live."

passageText: There is a critical factor that determines whether your choice will influence that of others: the visible consequences of the choice. Take the case of the Adélie penguins. They are often found strolling in large groups toward the edge of the water in search of food. Yet danger awaits in the icy-cold water. There is the leopard seal, for one, which likes to have penguins for a meal. What is an Adélie to do? The penguins' solution is to play the waiting game. They wait and wait and wait by the edge of the water until one of them gives up and jumps in. The moment that occurs, the rest of the penguins watch with anticipation to see what happens next. If the pioneer survives, everyone else will follow suit. If it perishes, they'll turn away. One penguin's destiny alters the fate of all the others. Their strategy, you could say, is "learn and live."

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E) 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We tend to go long periods of time without reaching out to the people we know.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: we suddenly take notice of the distance that has formed and we scramble to make repairs

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We call people which we haven't spoken to in ages, hoping that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: This isn't to say that you shouldn't bother calling someone just because it's been a while since you've spoken

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: just that it's more ideal not to let yourself fall out of touch in the first place

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 전치사 without 뒤에는 동명사가 와야 하므로 'reaching out to'는 올바른 형태이다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 'This isn't to say that...'는 '~라는 말은 아니다'라는 의미의 to부정사 관용 표현으로 어법상 적절하다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 사역동사 let은 목적격보어로 원형부정사를 취하므로 'let yourself fall out of touch'는 올바른 목적격보어 구조이다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 과거에 시작되어 현재까지 영향을 미치는 상태를 나타내므로 현재완료 'has formed'는 시제상 적절하다.

question.explanation: 밑줄 (C) 'which we haven't spoken to'는 선행사 people을 수식하는 목적격 관계절이다. 선행사 people은 사람이므로 사물을 가리키는 관계대명사 which를 쓸 수 없어 어법상 틀렸다. 사람 선행사에는 who(m) 또는 that을 쓰거나, 목적격 관계대명사이므로 생략하여 'people we haven't spoken to'로 써야 한다. 따라서 'which we haven't spoken to'를 'we haven't spoken to'(관계대명사 생략)로 고쳐야 한다. 관계대명사 자리에서 선행사의 종류(사람/사물)를 확인하지 않고 넘기기 쉬운 함정이다.
keyPoints: (C) 관계사 — 선행사가 사람(people)이면 which를 쓸 수 없다
(B) 수일치·시제 — 현재완료 has formed는 과거부터 현재까지 지속된 상태를 나타내 적절하다
(A) 준동사 — 전치사 without 뒤에는 동명사가 와야 하므로 reaching out to가 적절하다
question.passageWithMarkers: We tend to go long periods of time without __(A) reaching out to__ the people we know. Then, we suddenly take notice of the distance that __(B) has formed__ and we scramble to make repairs. We call people __(C) which we haven't spoken to__ in ages, hoping that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created. However, this rarely works: relationships aren't kept up with big one-time fixes. They're kept up with regular maintenance, like a car. In our relationships, we have to make sure that not too much time goes by between oil changes, so to speak. This __(D) isn't to say__ that you shouldn't bother calling someone just because it's been a while since you've spoken; just that it's more ideal not __(E) to let yourself__ fall out of touch in the first place. Consistency always brings better results.

passageText: We tend to go long periods of time without reaching out to the people we know. Then, we suddenly take notice of the distance that has formed and we scramble to make repairs. We call people we haven't spoken to in ages, hoping that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created. However, this rarely works: relationships aren't kept up with big one-time fixes. They're kept up with regular maintenance, like a car. In our relationships, we have to make sure that not too much time goes by between oil changes, so to speak. This isn't to say that you shouldn't bother calling someone just because it's been a while since you've spoken; just that it's more ideal not to let yourself fall out of touch in the first place. Consistency always brings better results.
